question_text: What is the main purpose of cross-validation in classification?
options: A. Feature selection | B. Model evaluation | C. Hyperparameter tuning | D. All of the above

question_text: What does the term "overfitting" refer to in the context of classification models?
options: A. The model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data | B. The model performs poorly on both training and unseen data | C. The model is perfectly generalized to any data | D. The model has too many parameters
correct_answer: The model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data

question_text: What does the term "false positive" represent in a confusion matrix?
options: A. Instances correctly identified as positive | B. Instances incorrectly identified as positive | C. Instances correctly identified as negative | D. Instances incorrectly identified as negative

question_text: What is the purpose of pruning in decision trees?
options: A. Increase model complexity | B. Reduce overfitting | C. Reduce the number of parameters | D. Reduce model interpretability

question_text: What is the disadvantage of decision trees?
options: A. Prone to overfitting | B. Not robust to outliers | C. Sensitive to feature scaling | D. Suitable for linear relationships only

question_text: Decision tree learners may create biased trees if some classes dominate. What’s the solution of it?
options: A. Balance the dataset prior to fitting | B. Imbalance the dataset prior to fitting | C. Balance the dataset after fitting | D. None of the above
correct_answer: Balance the dataset prior to fitting

question_text: Which of the following is a disadvantage of leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV)?
options: A. High computational cost | B. Overestimation of model performance | C. Limited model generalization | D. Biased toward larger datasets

question_text: What is the advantage of using cross-validation over a single train-test split?
options: A. It guarantees a larger training set | B. It provides multiple evaluations and provides a robust estimation | C. It speeds up the training process | D. It simplifies the model evaluation process
correct_answer: It provides multiple evaluations and provides a robust estimation

question_text: What does the term "stratified cross-validation" refer to?
options: A. Ensuring an equal distribution of target classes in each fold | B. Prioritizing one class over others during validation | C. Excluding certain features from the validation set | D. Randomly shuffling the data before splitting
correct_answer: Ensuring an equal distribution of target classes in each fold

question_text: Which of the following is a method to handle imbalanced class distribution in decision trees?
options: A. Feature scaling | B. Stratified sampling | C. Random shuffling | D. Increasing the tree depth

question_text: Which of the following is a hyperparameter of Decision Trees:
options: A. Tree depth | B. Minimum number of samples in leafs | C. Minimum number of samples to split nodes | D. All of the above

question_text: Which of the following methods can help to fine-tune tree depth in Decision Trees:
options: A. Trial and error | B. Random search | C. Learning curve | D. All of the above

question_text: Which of the following metrics can be used with a dataset having unbalanced classes:
options: A. Accuracy | B. F-Score | C. Precision | D. All of the above

question_text: How can you detect underfitting from a learning curve?
options: A. Bad results in train, but good results in test | B. Good results in train, but bad results in test | C. Bad results in both train and test | D. None of the above
correct_answer: Bad results in both train and test

question_text: Which of the following can be a reason for overfitting:
options: A. Insufficient training data | B. Excessive model complexity | C. Too many training iterations | D. All of the above

question_text: Which of the following can be a reason for underfitting:
options: A. Insufficient model complexity | B. Excessive training data | C. Too many training epochs | D. All of the above

question_text: Which of the following is true about non-parametric models as compared to parametric models:
options: A. They don't make prior assumptions on data's probability distribution | B. They are often more flexible and achieve better accuracy | C. They require more training data | D. All of the above

question_text: How can we handle the problem of underfitting in decision trees:
options: A. Increase the size of the tree | B. Add more attributes | C. Increase the size of the data | D. All of the above

question_text: Which of the following evaluation methods is not appropriate if the size of the data is small?
options: A. Holdout Method | B. Cross-validation | C. Leave-One-Out Approach | D. All of the above

question_text: What is a decision boundary in the context of decision trees?
options: A. Rectilinears that separate different classes in the feature space | B. The point at which a decision tree splits the data | C. A measure of the complexity of a decision tree | D. All of the above
correct_answer: Rectilinears that separate different classes in the feature space

question_text: The highest possible value of the Gini index for a set containing n different types of objects is:
options: A. 0 | B. 1 | C. log(n) | D. None of the above

question_text: The highest possible value of the miss classification error rate for a set containing n different types of objects is:
options: A. 0 | B. 1 | C. (n-1)/n | D. None of the above

question_text: If we use both Information gain and Gini gain to select the best split in a continuous variable, then:
options: A. We may find the same split position, as both measures (Gini and entropy) are consistent. | B. We might find different split positions even though the measures (Gini and entropy) are consistent. | C. We cannot find the same split positions, as the measures (Gini and entropy) used are inconsistent. | D. We may find different split positions because the measures (Gini and entropy) used are inconsistent.
correct_answer: We might find different split positions even though the measures (Gini and entropy) are consistent.

question_text: Which scenario allows a decision tree to split all training data into pure leaves?
options: A. When some samples have identical attributes but belong to different classes. | B. Splitting into pure leaves is not possible. | C. If two examples belong to different classes, they must have at least one differing attribute.
correct_answer: If two examples belong to different classes, they must have at least one differing attribute.

question_text: How does a decision tree classify an example after training if it encounters a new attribute value that was not considered in a splitting condition?
options: A. The example is not classified. | B. The most frequent class at the current node is assigned to the example | C. A random value from the supported attribute values is chosen, and the classification process continues. | D. None of the above
correct_answer: The most frequent class at the current node is assigned to the example

question_text: How does a decision tree manage an example with a missing value in a splitting condition during the testing phase?
options: A. The most common branch is chosen for the missing value. | B. The example is not classified. | C. A random value from the supported attribute values is chosen, and the classification process continues. | D. None of the above
correct_answer: The most common branch is chosen for the missing value.

question_text: How can overfitting be addressed in decision trees?
options: A. Use of post-pruning. | B. Use of pre-pruning. | C. Using as voting among multiple decision trees. | D. All of the above.

question_text: To set a baseline for determining if a classifier is acceptable, which of the following could be utilized?
options: A. The number of training examples in the minority class divided by the total number of training examples. | B. The inverse of the number of classes (1 divided by the number of classes) | C. The number of training examples in the majority class divided by the total number of training examples | D. None of the above
correct_answer: The number of training examples in the majority class divided by the total number of training examples

question_text: Why does a decision tree struggle with oblique splits?
options: A. Oblique splits are nonlinear. | B. It results from underfitting. | C. Only a single attribute is evaluated in each split condition. | D. All of the above.
correct_answer: Only a single attribute is evaluated in each split condition.

question_text: When providing a probability estimate for an example's classification using a decision tree, which method would be used?
options: A. The probability is estimated based on the class frequencies in the leaf node where the example is classified. | B. The probability is considered 1, as the path to this node indicates certainty in the majority class occurrence. | C. The probability is derived using the entropy at the leaf node where the classification occurs. | D. None of the above
correct_answer: The probability is estimated based on the class frequencies in the leaf node where the example is classified.
